title: Annotated reads: inference patterns and operational gotchas
content:
Quick annotated reading log + rough mental models for patterns that keep cropping up in infra work. Not a literature survey — more like a developer's cheat-sheet with open questions and quick TODOs.

Context / why I wrote this:
- Been pairing with SRE on a couple customer incidents where inference tail latency spiked after a model rollout. Wanted a compact map of the recurring causes and simple checks to run in the wild.
- Also collecting pointers for our next on-call rotation doc and a small postmortem template.

Top-level patterns (high-level):
1) Cold KV cache + heavy prefix skew -> initial latency storm
   - Symptom: first 10 requests per node 10x slower than steady-state.
   - Quick check: request id distribution + kv-hit-rate dashboard for that node/route.
   - Fixes to try (fast): warm simple prefixes from realtime traces, pre-warm on rollout.
   - Longer-term: TTL adaptive prefetch based on prefix popularity signal.
2) Quantization mismatch across variants -> subtle quality regressions
   - Symptom: customers see hallucination rate increase after switching to 4-bit variant; token-level perplexity ok but end-task metrics dip.
   - Hypothesis: distribution shift in intermediate activations causing attention-head sensitivity.
   - Proposed experiment: run paired scoring (FP16 vs Q4) on a prompt corpus; log token-level divergence + calibration histograms.
3) Microbatching-induced tail variance
   - Symptom: 95th+ latency jumps when request sizes vary; batching improves throughput but mixes short/long sequences causing head-of-line blocking.
   - Quick mitigation: size-aware batching (max tokens per batch) and strict queue isolation for latency-sensitive routes.
4) Routing fallbacks causing cold-start amplification
   - Symptom: when primary model OOMs during an autoscale event, fallback to larger-but-slower variant; sudden surge in latency and queueing.
   - Notes: our fallback table currently picks smallest-compat variant; maybe we should pick variant with similar seq-length perf instead.

Papers & short takeaways (annotated):
- "Efficient KV Caching for Transformer Inference" (arXiv 2023) - useful framing of cache coherence cost. Implementation detail to borrow: hierarchical cache eviction by prefix trie rather than pure LRU.
- "Batching Strategies for Low-Latency Inference" (conference talk, MSys 2026) - introduced size-aware binning approach (group by effective token budget). I should try a prototype in the dev cluster.
- "Quantization and QA calibration" (blog post) - practical tip: calibrate on representative prompts, not generic language modeling corpus.

Concrete quick experiments to run (next 2 weeks):
- EXP-avi-01: Paired scoring script (FP16 vs Q4) on 2k prompt set from customer X. Metrics: token divergence, BLEU/EM for QA, and per-head attention L2 shifts. Link: github PR in linked_artifacts.
- EXP-avi-02: Microbatch sim harness: replay production trace at different batching policies (size-aware, strict-isolate, dynamic-slice). Measure p50/p95/p99 and queue length distributions.
- EXP-avi-03: Rollout-warm strategy: on canary start, push top-100 prefixes to KV cache; compare 10-minute error/latency delta vs control.

Notes from pairing session with SRE (2027-02-12):
- Observed correlation between network interface queue depth and measured kv-read latency spikes. Might be noisy NIC drivers on older instances.
- We should add per-io-path histograms to the trace (nvme vs network) to attribute latency.

Open questions (unsolved):
- Is there a cheap metric that predicts when quantization will change downstream task quality? Current proxies (perplexity, L2) are noisy.
- How often do we need to refresh pre-warmed prefixes to avoid staleness without using excessive bandwidth?
- Can we dynamically route to a model variant based on an online estimate of token-sensitivity for the incoming prompt?

Housekeeping / things to file:
- File follow-up RFC: "Canary cache warm procedure" (owner: Avi) - link to create JIRA.
- Add new dashboard panel: "kv-prefix-hit-rate by top-10 prefixes" (owner: Hannah).
- Add EXP-avi-02 to weekly demo (03/01).

Snippets/cheat commands for on-call (put near runbook):
- curl our-trace-api/trace?reqid=<id> -> returns kv-hit events and model-variant.
- python tools/paired_score.py --fp16 --q4 --prompts=sample.json --out=diffs.csv

Random notes / brain dump (feel free to ignore):
- I keep thinking of a lightweight "sensitivity fingerprint" for a prompt: a small vector capturing which attention heads and layers the prompt activates most. Could be used to pick model variant or route preference.
- If we can cheaply estimate prompt-shaped burstiness (e.g., many long-context follow-ups), we could pre-allocate slice capacity.

References to save: 
- arXiv "Efficient KV Caching" https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05510
- MSys 2026 talk slides (internal copy): link pinned in slack #ml-systems (ask Owen).

Status: rough draft. Will refine after experiments.

-- Avi
